note: THE-340 moves rota invitations and reminders off the church's own Gmail onto Resend, from a Harvest-controlled sender on the verified theharvest.app domain, so a church that has connected NOTHING can still reach its volunteers. Digests are the state THE-340 leaves each file at, APPENDED to the accepted set rather than substituted for anyone else's entry — main went red once when a PR replaced a pinned digest instead of appending. No firestore.rules digest is recorded here, deliberately: this ticket does not touch that file, and every access to the rotaInvitations collection goes through the Admin SDK, which bypasses rules entirely. firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and src/app/layout.tsx are likewise untouched and unrecorded. THREE FILES THIS TICKET CHANGED ARE DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED ABOVE, and the omission is structural rather than substantive. The third is src/__tests__/THE-325.rules-digest-register.test.ts, where the only change is PINNING_SUITES 59 -> 60 for the new pinning suite, the accepted digest set untouched. The other two are the lib suites whose premises this ticket reverses: src/lib/__tests__/THE-324.rota-send.test.ts, whose composio-client stub became a stub of the resend package and whose 'with no Gmail connection either, the invitation still exists to be shared by hand' case is inverted into 'a volunteer receives an invitation with NOTHING connected'; and the THE-335 rota email-only suite, which pinned the defect outright with a case asserting rota mail goes through the church's Gmail 'not through Resend', and whose Gmail scope guard grepped rota-invite.ts for an identifier that file never called or imported — the only occurrence was a prose comment, so it would have passed with the real function deleted; it now CALLS the function against the scope sets that must be refused. Neither path can be listed in an entries[].file field because both carry another ticket's name, and THE-322's index guard reads any ticket name in a structural field as a record listing another record. That guard is correct to refuse an index and is left exactly as it is; naming these two here in prose is the same provenance the register already expects a 'why' to carry. The same collision applies to THE-325's own suite path. It is worth recording as a blind spot for a later ticket rather than worked around here: because this repository names test files after the ticket that wrote them, ANY ticket that legitimately edits another ticket's suite is unable to pin that file's digest in its own record, and the more files a ticket touches across other tickets' suites the more of its work goes unpinned. Widening the guard to look at path SEGMENTS rather than substrings, or to ignore a ticket name that appears inside a .test.ts filename, would close it without weakening the index refusal it exists for. THE-340 does not make that change: it is another ticket's guard, and altering it to admit this ticket's records is exactly the move the register's own notes warn against.

entries.why: THE-340 owns this change and it is the ticket: the email half moved off the church's own Gmail onto Resend. sendOneEmail no longer reads the tenant's Gmail integration document, no longer calls executeComposioAction and no longer passes from_email (Composio needed it because resolving a sender is a Gmail PROFILE read, gated behind a mailbox scope Harvest deliberately does not hold; Resend sends from a domain Harvest owns, so there is no profile to read). It calls sendTransactionalEmail instead, which keeps the module's stated import discipline: no provider is imported here and nothing is fetched. adminUid was dropped from sendInvitation because the Gmail connection document was its only reader. The record-first order, the token preservation rule, recordResponse's two-field scope and the SMS half are all untouched.

THE-340 adds this file, and the decision behind it is recorded in its own header. Every existing Resend path was read first: nine are inline `new Resend(key)` constructions at the point of use, and two of the eleven named in the brief (AdminAccounting.tsx, money-path-sentry.ts) do not send at all — one renders a button labelled Resend Email, the other names the vendor in prose. None is a function that could be called, so the real choice was between inlining a tenth copy inside rota-invite.ts — which would construct a new client AND put a provider import in a file whose discipline is that it holds none — and giving the copies the funnel they never had. This is that funnel, shaped after sms-send.ts's sendTenantSms. The nine existing call sites are deliberately NOT rewritten; four are money paths. An absent RESEND_API_KEY is reported as a failure here rather than skipped silently, because for rota mail that skip is the Silent-Failure Rule's quiet lie.

THE-340 owns this one-line change: sendInvitation no longer takes adminUid, so the call no longer passes user.uid. Nothing else in the route moved — the batch ceiling, the master-switch read ahead of the plan cell, the truncation refusal and the per-result reporting are all untouched.

THE-340 adds this suite. It holds the shape properties of the change — which funnel was reused, that rota-invite.ts still constructs no client and imports no provider, what an admin is told when a send fails (including the two cases a try/catch alone would miss: the provider resolving with an error object, and an unset API key), the accept link's URL shape and its two-field write scope, that no marketing gate catches transactional mail, and that no volume ceiling was invented. The end-to-end behaviour lives in the two lib suites this ticket also updated.

THE-340 owns this change. Section 13's third case asserted that the rota email half names the Composio Gmail action, passes from_email, and reaches Composio exactly once. Those three had no subject left once the transport moved, so they are replaced by their strengthened form: the rota path names that action ZERO times and reaches Composio ZERO times, which is strictly less than the one send-only call it used to make, and it goes through the transactional funnel instead. The section's own property — that this feature must not call the scope guard, weaken it, or ask for a wider grant — is unchanged, and the behavioural case that RUNS the guard against refused scope sets was already here and is untouched.

THE-340 owns this append and nothing else in the file. RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 59 -> 60 and this ticket's suite is added to RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-337's entry, never over it — which is the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules. No accepted value is widened and no pinner is retired.
